question: What is the refusal gate?
gold_answer: The refusal gate is a relevance floor on the retrieval side: it can refuse a question before the model is called at all. A question with no support in the corpus therefore costs zero model calls and produces zero generated text, so there is nothing that can be wrong. It scores two channels — a dense one and a lexical one — combines them into a single number and compares that number to a threshold measured against your own corpus by npx docpilot calibrate. Of the four stages that can end a turn, three end it before any model is reached, and the gate is one of those three. A refusal placed after generation is one you have already paid for; placing it first is what makes it measurable.

question: What are the two channels the gate scores a question on?
gold_answer: The dense channel measures how far the best in-scope chunk stands out. With a cosine-trained embedding model the absolute value is calibrated and can be thresholded directly; with an anisotropic one it cannot, and a shift-free statistic is used instead. The index records which instrument it was built for, so changing embedding model cannot silently inherit the wrong one. The lexical channel measures what share of the question rarest terms appear in the retrieved text, with the term count capped so the measure stays length-invariant. An unlisted term counts as maximally rare. The two are combined with weights, and the lexical weight is asserted at startup to be below the threshold, so rare identifiers plus an off-domain ask cannot clear the gate alone. The dense channel may pass on its own.

question: Is the free tier limited by requests or by tokens?
gold_answer: By requests per day, not tokens. Under ten lifetime credits bought the cap is fifty free-model requests per day; at ten credits or more it is a thousand, and there is always a ceiling of twenty requests per minute. The daily counter covers model ids ending in :free, and openrouter/free — the router at the head of the shipped pool — carries no such suffix but is not exempt either. The window ends at midnight UTC. This matters because the intuitive fix is the wrong one: free models publish context windows of 128k to 512k, so splitting a question into more calls to make it fit solves a problem you do not have, and each extra call is one of the fifty. The dashboard will not warn you, because spend stays at zero while you are fully blocked.

question: What does the docpilot index command do?
gold_answer: It builds the retrieval index into docs/public/rag, or wherever indexDir points. The build is idempotent: identical input produces byte-identical output. Two flags change what it does. --dry chunks and reports without embedding — no network and no model — which is the loop for tuning chunking. --no-embed writes a real index with no vectors in it: no embedding calls, no vectors blob, and retrieval by BM25 alone. That flag alone is not a deployable state; a vectorless index under a config that still names an embedder is a readiness failure rather than a warning, doctor reports it, and such a site ships with the panel disabled. When you named a provider but no model, index also asks the provider which embedding models it serves and lines its answers up behind the configured name.

question: How do I install DocPilot in a VitePress site?
gold_answer: Two halves, and only one of them cares what your site is built with. In docs/.vitepress/config.mjs import defineDocPilot, call it with loadEnv, and pass ai.plugin() into vite.plugins and ai.themeConfig into themeConfig.docPilot. Put one provider key in .env.local. Then wrap the theme: in docs/.vitepress/theme/index.js export withDocPilot(DefaultTheme) from @cloflin/docpilot/theme, or re-export the packaged theme directly if you have no theme of your own. Finally run npx docpilot index to build the retrieval index and npx docpilot calibrate to measure the refusal thresholds against your corpus. The index does not need a site at all — it walks markdown and writes static files — while the panel needs a page that can tell it what is configured, what page this is and what language it is in.

question: Where should the API key live?
gold_answer: In Node, and never in the page. themeConfig is compiled into the client bundle, so a key written there is a key published. In development the Vite plugin installs a proxy that attaches the key server-side. In production your own reverse proxy does the same thing, and the built site expects a same-origin /ai path in front of it. One consequence catches people out: vitepress preview has no proxy, so the panel cannot answer there. That is not a bug to work around by moving the key into the config — it is the contract working as intended. Put the key in .env.local, which the loader reads, and let the proxy carry it.

question: What is the answer ladder?
gold_answer: It is the order in which a turn tries to produce an answer, and the guarantee that it never ends empty-handed. By the time anything can fail, the question has been embedded, both retrieval channels have run, the gate has scored it and every ranked passage is already in memory — none of which needed a model. Rung one walks every provider your keys select, billed accounts first, moving on when one returns 429, 5xx, 401 or a network error. Rung two is a provider own free catalogue, and a server of your own comes last. Rung three is not a service at all: it is retrieval thinning out to lexical-only beneath whichever rung answered. Rung four is what the reader sees when nothing answered — the passages the turn already retrieved, linked, under one sentence.

question: What is the capital of France?
How do I configure Algolia DocSearch crawling for my site?
What does the docpilot index command do?
How much conversation memory does the assistant keep?
gold_answer: Three question-answer pairs travel verbatim; earlier questions collapse into a single line naming their subjects. Answers are truncated, and only turns that actually completed are carried — an empty assistant message is not a neutral placeholder, and two refused turns ahead of an answerable one were measured turning it into a refusal. The summary line is built from prior questions only, never from answer text, because a memory slot the model authors itself and that outlives the window is a multi-turn injection channel the gate cannot see. The gate keeps the same rule one step earlier: its composed channel composes the follow-up against the last question that was answered, not the last one asked. Truncation to 300 characters is also why a reader can quote a passage forward into the next question.

question: What exactly is stored in conversation history, and where?
gold_answer: Per turn: the question as it was redacted, the quoted passage if the reader attached one, the answer text with its source links and any vote, and the scope plus the gate numbers a feedback report reads. Not stored: the model reasoning, the retrieved excerpts, the rendered HTML — recomputed on restore, which is both smaller and more correct — and the reader own added instruction, which stays in sessionStorage and dies with the tab. It lives in two keys in two storages: docpilot:history in localStorage is the archive shared by every tab, and docpilot:conversation in sessionStorage records which conversation this tab is showing. Both are on the reader device under your origin and neither is ever sent anywhere. The only thing that leaves the browser is a vote, and only when feedbackEndpoint is configured.

question: What happens if a reader pastes an API key into the question box?
gold_answer: The question settles locally with zero network calls of any kind. The reader is told, in their own language, that the value was not sent anywhere and is not kept in the thread, and is offered a button that resubmits the same question with the value already replaced by a placeholder. Detection is by shape over the raw question: prefixed API keys, JWTs, Bearer headers, AWS key ids, and any run of thirty-two or more hex characters. A bare UUID is deliberately not matched, because plugin, template, message and account ids are all UUIDs and warning in front of ordinary questions trains readers to click through. It is a habit guard, not a security boundary: everything runs in the reader browser and it cannot stop someone pasting a key into a model directly.

question: Why are the vectors quantised, and what does it cost?
gold_answer: Chunk vectors are stored as int8, which is the difference between an index a browser downloads and one it does not. Every vector is L2-normalised, then each dimension becomes round(v x 127) clamped to plus or minus 127 — one signed byte per dimension, with no per-vector scale or offset stored anywhere. Because the vectors are normalised, cosine is the dot product, so the browser scores with integer arithmetic over one flat Int8Array and divides once by 127 squared at the end. The blob is a single file exactly chunkCount x dims bytes long, and the store throws rather than scoring a truncated download. The cost is measured rather than assumed: every build samples up to two hundred vector pairs and prints the mean absolute cosine difference. Above 0.01 the build dies instead of writing the index.

question: How do I scope a question to part of the docs?
gold_answer: A chip in the composer opens a picker offering All docs, This page, This section, or a hand-picked list of pages. Over roughly a dozen pages a filter field appears above the list, controlled by scope.filter, and the pages are grouped by section. What a scope means is focus rather than containment: the assistant is shown only chunks from the active scope, through every tool it has, but a scope is a retrieval decision and not a security one. Where a fresh conversation starts is set by scope.default. When a scoped question is refused the panel offers Closest pages elsewhere and a button to clear the scope and search all docs, so a scope that turned out to be too narrow is one click to escape.

question: What does the reader see when the assistant refuses?
gold_answer: A refusal is not an error and does not look like one. The panel says what it searched and what it did not find, then does the useful thing: it lists the closest pages — the best chunks that fell under the threshold — as links. Under a narrow scope it also offers Closest pages elsewhere plus a button to clear the scope and search all docs. It reports what the turn actually did, in the form of a line saying it searched the docs and read some number of pages, so the refusal is checkable. If the semantic index could not be loaded and only word matching ran, a separate sentence says degraded, because that is a different fact from not in the docs. Nothing was generated and nothing was spent.

question: What does the panel do if I just say hello?
gold_answer: The turn settles in the browser with no model call. The reader gets a greeting in their own language that names the product, says what kinds of question the pages cover, and repeats the suggestion rows so there is something to act on — an invitation with nothing to act on is the refusal it was written to replace. The reply is a template, not a generation, for three reasons in order of weight: a model handed no evidence is exactly the configuration that invents product behaviour, and hello is not worth that risk; the copy is reader-facing UI and belongs in a diff where it can be reviewed; and a greeting costs zero tokens instead of a round trip. Temperature is therefore not a lever here and never will be, because nothing is sampled.

question: How does the i18n fallback work?
gold_answer: Per leaf, down an ordered list of five places. First the translations for the selected locale, then the top-level translations block. For reply keys only there is a third step: the translations of the site own locale, on the reasoning that a reader typing an unrecognised language on a Russian site is better served Russian than English. Then the shipped default for that locale, and finally the shipped default for English. Because the fallback runs per leaf rather than per object, a partial translation is legal — you supply the keys you have and every key you left out resolves down the chain. A regional tag is normalised to its subtag, so ru-RU finds ru and en-US finds en. A locale nobody ships and nobody configured falls back to English rather than rendering blank.

question: What is the provider chain and how does it pick a service?
gold_answer: chat.provider ships as auto, which reads your environment: it walks an ordered list and stops at the first service a key is set for, bringing that service own default model with it, and embed: auto follows it into the retrieval half. One key in .env.local is the whole configuration. Embed-capable providers come first — openai, gemini, mistral, together, fireworks, nebius, openrouter — then the chat-only ones such as anthropic, groq, deepseek, xai and cerebras. The three local entries are selected by an address rather than a key: custom by CUSTOM_BASE_URL, llamacpp by LLAMACPP_BASE_URL and ollama by OLLAMA_BASE_URL. When nothing matches at all the chain falls through to openrouter on its free tier.

question: How do I use the docpilot deploy command?
How do I write a Kubernetes admission webhook?
Where should the API key live?
What does DocPilot guarantee about every answer?
gold_answer: Four things hold for every answer, for every model, under every prompt including one you have edited. They are enforced by host code no message can reach, and each is covered by a test. Every source link points at a page that exists in the index — enforced in the markdown-it token stream on a normalised path compared by set membership, before anything is rendered, so an invented route is de-linked and left as plain text. When retrieval finds nothing above the threshold no answer is generated, because the model is never called. The assistant is shown only chunks from the active scope, through priming, search, fetch, listing and section expansion alike. And every citation shown corresponds to a chunk the host itself put in front of the model during that turn, checked against a set the host maintains.

question: How does retrieval fuse its two channels?
gold_answer: Retrieval is hybrid and both halves always run. A BM25 pass over the chunk text, the title and the breadcrumb — with the title weighted — and a cosine pass over the int8 vectors produce two ranked lists, and the two are merged by Reciprocal Rank Fusion: each list contributes 1/(k + rank) to every id it names and the sums are sorted. Ranks, not scores, which is what lets two channels with incomparable units vote in the same election. The fused pool is then re-ranked by dense cosine before the gate sees it. Note that fusion weights both channels equally: the wDense 0.75 and wLexical 0.25 in the manifest are the gate weights, a different stage scoring a different thing. With no embedder reachable the dense list is simply empty and BM25 runs alone.

question: Why is the import allowlist a security boundary?
gold_answer: Because docPilot.sources.allow decides which origins a source may name, and that value travels from frontmatter into manifest.pages origin, into the source row, and out as an href rendered inside the answer panel. Without a gate, a javascript: URL hand-written into any markdown file in the repository would be stored XSS. So the rules are strict: https only, by allowlist rather than denylist, because javascript:, data: and vbscript: are the ones with names and the next one is the one nobody named. Origins are compared as origins, which defeats both example.com.evil.test and example.com@evil.test. A path prefix narrows at a segment boundary, so /docs admits /docs/anything and rejects /docsecret. A source outside the list fails the build with the page named. Absent is legal; malformed is not.

question: Which blocks will the chunker never cut through?
gold_answer: Heading structure and the 500-token target are preferences; the 8,000-character ceiling named MAX_CHUNK_CHARS is the law, and a section over it is split whatever its structure. What the splitter guarantees is that the structure survives the cut. A fenced code block is never left unterminated: a fence over the ceiling is closed at the cut and reopened on the next part with the same fence characters, the same indent and the same info string, and the room for that repair is reserved so a repaired part cannot itself be re-cut. A table is never left with unlabelled rows: it is cut between rows and every continuation re-emits the header and the delimiter. Neither is broken at the preference boundary either, and the one block of overlap that carries continuity across a seam applies only when the trailing block is prose.

question: How do I quote a passage into the composer?
gold_answer: Select text and a single button appears above the selection. Pressing it attaches the passage to the composer as a removable chip, so the question can be what does this mean with a this actually on screen. Inside an answer the behaviour is on by default, controlled by quote.fromAnswer. Over your own prose it is off by default, controlled by quote.fromDocs, because painting a selection control on your article is a decision about your site rather than about the panel. The quote is carried with that question one turn later, clamped shorter, and it is redacted on the same credential rule as the question itself and capped at 500 characters when it is written to history.

question: How do I mount DocPilot in React?
gold_answer: Import DocPilotPanel from @cloflin/docpilot/react and the stylesheet from @cloflin/docpilot/web.css, then render the panel inside your layout, passing it the config and the current route. The config normally arrives on the page as a global the build wrote, and the route is whatever your router calls the current pathname — the panel needs it because it answers about the page the reader is on. The React entry point imports a prebuilt bundle rather than source, which is what keeps the panel out of your own build graph. The index half is unaffected by any of this: npx docpilot index walks markdown and writes static files, and knows nothing about React.

question: Which syntax highlighter does DocPilot use by default?
gold_answer: None is installed by default, and that is deliberate. A default inside the package would put a Shiki import into every consumer module graph, and a bundler that cannot resolve it fails the build — so a Docusaurus site that chose Prism would still have to install Shiki in order to compile. You choose one by calling setHighlighter once, before the panel is first opened. The VitePress entry point calls it for you with Shiki, and mountDocPilot takes a highlighter as an option. Everywhere else you call it yourself. With no highlighter every code block renders as a plain escaped block with its copy button, which is the same thing an unsupported language already produces, so it is a shape the panel is designed around rather than a broken state.

question: Почему шлюз отказывает до вызова модели?
gold_answer: Шлюз — это порог релевантности на стороне поиска, а не проверки ответа. Вопрос, у которого нет опоры в корпусе, стоит нуля вызовов модели и порождает нуль сгенерированного текста: ошибаться попросту нечему. Из четырёх стадий, способных завершить оборот, три завершают его до того, как модель вообще достигнута — проверка учётных данных, социальное приветствие и сам шлюз. Отказ, поставленный после генерации, — это отказ, за который уже заплачено токенами и текстом, который на мгновение существовал. Постановка его первым — то, что делает отказ измеримым. Порог не выбирается вручную: его меряет npx docpilot calibrate против вашего собственного корпуса, а не чужого.

question: What is topK and what is its default?
gold_answer: topK is how many excerpts the gate hands the model to open a turn with — the retriever GATE_K under its documented name, and the k every retrieval number in an eval report is measured at. Its type is number or null and its default is null. Nothing read this key until recently: it was documented from the first release with a default of 12 while the gate k was a literal 5 in the retriever, so 5 is what every site actually retrieved with whatever the key said. It is wired up now, and its default is null rather than a number because no single number is right for every corpus. null means use what this corpus measured: docpilot tune sweeps the k against your golden set, index inlines the winner into the manifest, and with no tuning present null resolves to 5.

question: What is the free pool and how does rotation inside it work?
gold_answer: Once the walk reaches a provider own free catalogue a second rotation starts inside that one member. Naming openrouter as the provider with no model gives an ordered pool of ten, headed by openrouter/free — OpenRouter own router over the free tier — with nine explicit free ids behind it. A free id is a shared allocation, so its 429 reports how many other people are asking rather than anything about the model, and pinning one buys a panel that works until somebody else traffic arrives. Both rotations are metered by requests per day rather than tokens: fifty under ten lifetime credits, a thousand over. A mixed chain turns per-day rationing off, because a free tier beside a metered account is two allowances against one counter; set budget.dailyLimit to state one ceiling.

question: What does chat.retryDelay default to?
How do I bake sourdough bread?
Why are the vectors quantised?
What is the Mintlify CLI command for a local preview?
What happens to retrieval when the embedder is unreachable?
gold_answer: This is not a service the walk reaches — it is the evidence half thinning out beneath whichever rung answered. The embedder is retried, then retrieval drops to lexical-only: BM25 alone over the chunk text, the title, the breadcrumb, the path and the anchor, with the gate switching to its lexical threshold. The dense list is simply empty and the model that answers is whichever one the walk above reached. It is a mode rather than a failure, and an expensive one: on a 1191-chunk corpus recall at 8 fell from 0.97 to 0.41. A site that declared lexical-only looks nothing like a site that lost its embedder — the first logs nothing, the second carries the reason in the console and says degraded on a refusal. What never happens is a second embedder.

question: What is a follow-up composed against?
prev_question: How much conversation memory does the assistant keep?
gold_answer: Against the last question that was answered, not the last one that was asked. A refused turn is a question this corpus retrieved nothing for, so putting it in front of the follow-up would anchor the one channel that could have recovered the turn to a known dead end. That is the same turn the memory window drops, and it is dropped for the same measured reason: two refused turns ahead of an answerable one were seen turning it into a refusal. The composition happens in the gate composed channel, one step earlier than the conversation window, and the summary line the window keeps is built from prior questions only rather than from answer text — a memory slot the model authors itself, outliving the window, would be a multi-turn injection channel the gate cannot see.

question: What does the calibrate command measure, and what may never move it?
gold_answer: It measures the refusal thresholds against your own corpus and writes them to the eval directory as calibration.json, with a report beside it. It needs the embed endpoint only: no chat model is ever contacted, because a threshold that moves when a generator moves is not a threshold, and there is no LLM judge anywhere in it. The four values it owns are tau, tauLexical, wDense and wLexical, and the only legal way to change any of them is to run calibrate again. A hand-set guard in your config is honoured but stamps the gate source as config on every record of the session. The result only takes effect at the next index, because that is the step which inlines the calibration into the manifest a reader downloads.

question: Why are the skills copied into my project rather than imported?
gold_answer: Because a skill inside node_modules reaches nobody: the .claude directory is discovered in the project, not in a dependency. Copying is the only delivery mechanism there is, which is why it happens as part of init rather than as a documented step somebody might skip. Once copied they are yours, and editing them is expected rather than discouraged — the numbers written into them describe the corpus this package was developed against, not yours. The corollary is the upgrade behaviour: an existing file is never overwritten, so a skill you have edited survives an upgrade, and by the same rule a skill that gained new material upstream does not update itself. Never overwriting cuts both ways, and that trade is stated rather than hidden.

question: Which two theme tokens does the stylesheet move on its own?
gold_answer: Two, and both are overrides written on root or body in the core stylesheet rather than defaults you are expected to set. The first is the z-index: below the sheet breakpoint at 959 pixels VitePress raises its own sidebar to 60 and its backdrop to 50, so a modal sheet left at 29 would render underneath the hamburger menu, and the core raises --dp-z to 70 in that media query. The second is the floating-button clearance: when there is no floating button on the page — an ordinary configuration if the trigger is nav and the panel is a popup — the popup reserves no room under itself by zeroing --dp-fab-clear. That rule is written as the absence of the button, so a browser without support for the has selector keeps the room, which is the miss in the safe direction.

question: Что хранится в истории переписки и где?
gold_answer: История лежит в двух ключах двух разных хранилищ. Ключ docpilot:history в localStorage — это архив: все разговоры, общие для всех вкладок сайта. Ключ docpilot:conversation в sessionStorage хранит лишь то, какой разговор показывает именно эта вкладка. Оба находятся на устройстве читателя, в origin вашего сайта, и никуда не отправляются. За оборот сохраняются: вопрос в том виде, в каком он был отредактирован маской, процитированный фрагмент, если читатель его прикрепил, текст ответа со ссылками на источники и голосом, а также область поиска и числа шлюза. Не сохраняются рассуждения модели, извлечённые фрагменты, отрендеренный HTML и собственная инструкция читателя. Единственное, что покидает браузер, — голос, и только если настроен feedbackEndpoint.

How do I set up a Terraform remote backend on S3?
How does the i18n fallback work?
What does the credential check deliberately not match, and why?
gold_answer: A bare UUID is deliberately not matched. Plugin ids, template ids, message ids and account ids are all UUIDs, and putting a warning in front of ordinary questions trains readers to click through it — which costs more than the UUID is worth. The wider argument is that the error is chosen rather than avoided: there is no oracle for a live credential, and the alternative to a shape test is no test at all. A false positive costs one click and then runs the question verbatim minus the matched span. A false negative is the failure the check exists to prevent. The patterns lean towards preventing the second, and the known collision — a forty-character git SHA, which the thirty-two-hex rule catches — is priced at that one click.

question: Why does the fusion weight both channels equally when the gate does not?
gold_answer: Because they are two different stages scoring two different things. Reciprocal Rank Fusion is deciding which chunks make the pool, and it works on ranks rather than scores precisely so that two channels with incomparable units can vote in the same election — weighting them unequally there would be asserting a unit conversion that does not exist. The gate is deciding whether the pool is good enough to answer from, and there wDense 0.75 against wLexical 0.25 is a calibrated statement about how much each channel is worth as evidence. The lexical weight is additionally asserted at startup to be below the threshold, so a query made of rare identifiers plus an off-domain ask cannot clear the gate with no dense evidence at all. The two numbers look alike and are not.

question: And what does the manifest record about the embedding model?
prev_question: What are the two channels the gate scores a question on?
gold_answer: It records which instrument the index was built for. The dense channel measures how far the best in-scope chunk stands out, and how that number may be read depends on the embedding model: with a cosine-trained model the absolute value is calibrated and can be thresholded directly, while with an anisotropic one it cannot and a shift-free statistic is used instead. Because the index writes down which of the two it was built for, changing the embedding model cannot silently inherit the wrong instrument — the mismatch is caught rather than quietly producing numbers that look plausible. That is the same reason retrieval degrades to a weaker channel rather than to a foreign vector space when an embedder goes away.

question: What does a --no-embed index cost me, in one number?
gold_answer: Recall at 8 measured 0.97 with vectors and 0.41 without, on a 1191-chunk corpus. That is the number to read before treating lexical-only as normal. The --no-embed flag writes a real index with no vectors in it: no embedding calls, no vectors blob, and retrieval by BM25 alone over the chunk text, the title, the breadcrumb, the path and the anchor, with the gate switching to its lexical threshold. The flag alone is not a deployable state, and that is the part to know first — a vectorless index under a config that still names an embedder is a readiness failure rather than a warning, doctor reports it, and a site built that way ships with the panel disabled entirely. Use the flag to look at the mode; set embed to false to run on it.

question: How does the allowlist defeat a lookalike origin?
gold_answer: By comparing origins as origins rather than by matching strings. That is what defeats both of the two classic lookalikes: a subdomain suffix such as example.com.evil.test, and a userinfo prefix such as example.com@evil.test — each of which contains the allowed host as a substring while resolving somewhere else entirely. A path prefix narrows further, and it narrows at a segment boundary, so an entry for example.com/docs admits /docs and /docs/anything while rejecting /docsecret. The scheme rule is separate and is an allowlist rather than a denylist: https only, because javascript:, data: and vbscript: are the ones with names and the next one is the one nobody named. A source outside the list fails the build with the page named.

question: What is reserved so a repaired chunk cannot be re-cut?
gold_answer: The room for the repair itself. When a fenced code block runs over the 8,000-character ceiling the splitter closes the fence at the cut and reopens it on the next part with the same fence characters, the same indent and the same info string. Those added characters are part of the chunk as it is embedded, so if the splitter had cut right up to the ceiling the repair would push the part back over it and the part would be re-cut at an arbitrary offset. Reserving the room in advance is what stops that. The same ceiling counts the Page and Section context line prepended to every chunk and the frontmatter description prepended to a page first chunk, because those are embedded too.

question: Which providers in the chain cannot embed?
gold_answer: Five of them: anthropic, groq, deepseek, xai and cerebras. They sit after the embed-capable entries in the chain for exactly that reason, since the chain is ordered with embed-capable providers first. The seven that do embed are openai, gemini, mistral, together, fireworks, nebius and openrouter, and the three address-selected local entries — custom, llamacpp and ollama — embed as well. This matters because embed: auto follows the chat provider, so naming a chat-only provider and leaving the embed half on auto has to resolve somewhere else. Naming such a provider explicitly for the embed half is a build-stopping error rather than a silent downgrade, and the alternatives are borrowing a free embedding pool or declaring embed: false and retrieving lexically.

question: Why does a greeting never reach a model?
gold_answer: Three reasons, given in order of weight. First, a model handed no evidence is exactly the configuration that invents product behaviour, and hello is not worth that risk. Second, the copy is reader-facing UI and belongs in a diff where it can be reviewed, rather than being regenerated differently on every visit. Third, a greeting costs zero tokens instead of a round trip. The reply is therefore a template rather than a generation, and the consequence is stated plainly: temperature is not a lever here and never will be, because nothing is sampled. The turn settles in the browser with no model call at all, and the suggestion rows are repeated in the greeting on purpose, since an invitation with nothing to act on is the refusal it was written to replace.

question: How many dimensions does the default embedder produce?
"The gate is a relevance floor, not an entailment check." Now translate that into Latin and explain the grammar.
What does DocPilot guarantee about every answer?
And what does the reader see when it refuses?
prev_question: How does the refusal gate decide?
gold_answer: A refusal is not styled as an error. The panel says what it searched and that it could not find the answer there, then does the useful thing: it lists the closest pages as links, the best chunks that fell under the threshold. Under a narrow scope it adds closest pages elsewhere and a single button that clears the scope and searches all the docs. It also says what the turn actually did, as in searched the docs and read four pages, so the refusal is checkable rather than a shrug. A separate sentence covers the degraded case, where the semantic index could not be loaded and only word matching ran, because that is a different fact from the answer not being in the docs. Nothing was generated and nothing was spent.

question: And which of them can embed?
gold_answer: Ten of them serve both halves, so naming the provider alone is a complete sentence: openai, together, fireworks, mistral, nebius, gemini, openrouter, ollama, llamacpp and custom. That is what the default embed auto relies on — it follows chat.provider and uses that provider's own embedding model, and every row above carries a default for each half. Those names are defaults rather than guarantees, because catalogues change and a stale one used to kill the index build on its first chunk with a 404 naming a model nobody typed. Two things stand behind them now. The embed half asks the provider which embedding models it actually serves and walks those answers behind the configured name, which is how custom and llamacpp stop being guesses about what you loaded. The chat half is asked by docpilot doctor --models.

question: How much of it survives a reload?
prev_question: Where does the panel keep the conversation history?
gold_answer: Reloading the page brings back the conversation that tab was in, including an answer that was still being written when the page went away. The list itself is the reader's own device and outlives the tab: a conversation appears in it once it has an answer, titled with the first question asked in it and dated relative to the last one. Opening a row switches the panel to that conversation and carries on in it. New chat lets go of the conversation on screen without deleting it, so it is still in the list. Delete removes one row, and deleting the conversation currently on screen empties the panel too. Delete all clears the list and the panel in one step, asking twice and never through a browser dialog.

question: And what makes it stop?
gold_answer: Two signals stop it outright, and everything else moves it along. The reader pressing stop, and a step timing out, stop the turn at both levels: the signal every later request inherits is already dead. Inside a pool a 401 stops as well, because a rejected key rejects every model behind it, and so does a network failure on the same socket and the day's 429, whose allowance belongs to the account. Across a provider boundary those same three continue instead, because the next provider is a different key, a different host and a second allowance. The minute's 429, a 5xx, a retired id, a moderation refusal and a 200 with no answer always move to the next member. Only the last member's daily 429 escapes, which is what keeps rate-limited a real state.

question: And which language does a reader get when nobody translated theirs?
prev_question: How do I translate the panel into another language?
gold_answer: It falls back per leaf, down a fixed order rather than per language. The locale's own translations are consulted first, then the root translations you configured, then — for the reply group only — any locale's translations, because a reader typing an unrecognised language on a Russian site is better served Russian than English. After that comes the shipped default for that locale, and last the shipped default for English. A regional tag is normalised to its subtag on the way in, so ru-RU finds ru and en-US finds en. A locale nobody ships and nobody configured lands on English rather than rendering blank, which is the property that makes a partial translation safe to deploy.

question: And what does the panel do when it runs out?
prev_question: What does the free tier actually meter?
gold_answer: It says the free daily limit is used up and when answers resume, taking the reset from the service's own answer rather than guessing at one. That is a distinct state rather than the generic message about the AI service not responding, which is reserved for a transport that failed — a service that told you exactly when to come back has not failed. Nothing is refused pre-emptively off the local count. A count that says zero can be wrong in the direction that costs a reader an answer the service would have given, so the panel asks and lets the service decide. The local number is used to shape the turn, not to veto it.

question: How do I add a cross-encoder reranker after the RRF fusion?
Which reranking model does the package ship?
How do I let a reader upload a PDF into the panel?
How do I make the panel answer from two indexes at once?
How do I fine-tune the embedding model on my own corpus?
How do I stream reader questions into a Slack channel?
How do I make the panel speak the answer out loud?
How do I index a Notion workspace with docpilot?
And when it is written in another alphabet?
prev_questions: How does the gate score a follow-up like «and for backend calls?»
What stops that from letting a topic switch through?
gold_answer: Then admissibility stands aside. The test asks whether a content word of the tail appears in the retrieved evidence, and over a corpus in another script the answer is no for every question such a reader could ask, on topic or off, so it stops measuring the subject and starts measuring the alphabet — discarding the one mechanism that resolves «and can I style it?» for exactly the readers who need it. So when no word of the tail is known to the corpus and the tail’s letters are not the corpus’s letters, the dense channel decides alone. It is not a pass: the composed score still has to beat the raw one and still has to clear the threshold, and the lexical weight sits below that threshold by assertion, so what gets a foreign tail through is dense evidence and nothing else. It does not travel to a vectorless deployment, where the remedy is vocabulary instead.

question: And why don't those two say what they searched?
prev_questions: In how many ways can a turn settle without an answer?
Which of them never reach the gate at all?
gold_answer: Because the line would describe work that did not happen. Both settle before retrieval runs, so “Searched the docs” would be false: a credential question is caught by a synchronous, network-free check and never leaves the browser, and a greeting is recognised and answered from a template. Neither one printing a provenance line is the honest outcome, not an omission. They still offer something — the credential case offers the same question with the value masked, and the social case offers what the assistant covers plus the suggestions. The three remaining causes sit behind a search that really ran, and one state, no-answer, covers all five. What none of them ever does is explain itself with a number: no score, no threshold, no “low confidence”, no “off-topic”.

question: And if none of them survive?
prev_questions: What checks run on an answer before the reader sees it?
What happens to a citation the model invented?
And to a link that points nowhere?
gold_answer: Then the answer is not shown at all. It becomes a refusal instead, because an uncited answer is exactly what the guardrail exists to withhold, and the turn settles as not-answerable — the model was called and returned nothing citable — with the closest pages offered in its place. Note what the test is: citation, not confidence. A low-confidence answer that is cited is kept and marked tentative, because confidence is the weakest signal in the system, a number the model writes about its own work. Deleting a checkable answer on that basis costs the whole turn and replaces something useful with a claim about the corpus that is not true. Surviving markers renumber, so a stripped citation leaves no gap behind it.

question: А сразу после него?
prev_questions: Сколько этапов проходит вопрос в панели, прежде чем читатель увидит ответ?
Сколько из них могут завершить ход до вызова модели?
А что делает третий?
gold_answer: Сразу после него идёт подготовленный ход. Если оценка оказалась выше порога, хост делает то, чего не делает большинство поисковых циклов: кладёт собственные выдержки гейта прямо в первое сообщение. Модель начинает с доказательствами на руках, а не тратит отдельный шаг на то, чтобы их запросить, — поэтому большинству ходов хватает одного вызова, а не двух. Если этот вызов не возвращается, дальше вступает лестница ответов: по очереди спрашивают каждый другой сервис, выбранный окружением. А ход, на который не ответил никто, оседает как те самые фрагменты, которые поиск уже нашёл, а не как извинение за них.

question: And the build?
prev_questions: How does OpenRouter's free tier limit what the panel can do?
What does one turn cost against that?
gold_answer: It draws on the same daily allowance, so a day spent answering readers' questions is a day the index cannot be rebuilt. The embedding pool is two models deep, and when both refuse the build says so and stops rather than leaving you a half-built index or a vectorless one nobody chose — you still have the index you had, and the site keeps working exactly as it did. Three ways out, in the order they cost you something. Wait: the allowance is a UTC day and the 429 carries X-RateLimit-Reset, and indexing a 300-chunk corpus is about ten requests of the next fifty. Raise the ceiling: ten credits take the daily limit from 50 to 1000, and set budget.dailyLimit to 1000 afterwards so the rationing rules know. Or declare embed.fallback: 'lexical', which builds a vectorless index instead of dying — read the cost first, because recall@8 falls from 0.97 to 0.41.

question: And what undoes that sorting?
prev_questions: How does DocPilot choose a provider when I have not named one?
What happens if my environment holds keys for two of them?
gold_answer: Naming a model, or writing your own chat.models list. A model you named keeps its provider billed: chat: {model: 'anthropic/claude-sonnet-4'} beside an OpenRouter key is a paid deployment, and the free catalogue answers only where nothing was named. Sinking that member would hand the model name to whichever provider sorted above it, which is a 404 for a model nobody typed there. So the tiers flatten and the order is the chain's own, unchanged — the table's order, the one the sort was there to correct. The sort fires exactly where the whole question is which of these keys, in what order, which is the zero-config path and nowhere else. The head is picked from the same sorted list, so chain[0] is chat.provider, and embed: 'auto' follows the member that leads rather than one the sort moved past.

question: Is it still necessary?
prev_questions: Can I use Anthropic as the chat provider?
Then what handles the retrieval half?
What does that cost me at build time?
gold_answer: Possibly not, and one command settles it rather than the table. That list of five providers with no embeddings endpoint is a claim this package wrote down, and claims age — the same table once said OpenRouter served no embeddings endpoint for months after it started. npx docpilot doctor --models asks your chat provider directly and says so when the answer has changed: groq answers /v1/embeddings after all, with nomic-embed-text-v1.5 named, and the note that embed: {provider: 'groq'} drops the borrowed openrouter key. It reports rather than switches, and the reason is worth knowing. The reverse proxy carrying /ai/v1/embeddings is written from your config at build time, so a build that moved itself would send every reader's query vector to the wrong upstream. You write that line yourself.

question: А если ни одна так и не ответила?
prev_questions: Что делает панель, когда бесплатная модель OpenRouter отказывает?
А отказавшая модель возвращается в пул?
Когда ротация не срабатывает?
gold_answer: Ход всё равно не заканчивается пустым. Он завершается состоянием results с выставленным turn.hybrid — это тот же поисковый продукт, что даёт chat: false, только достигнутый во время выполнения, а не настройкой: те же ранжированные строки, каждая дословная выдержка под ссылкой на заголовок, из которого её вырезали, а над ними одна фраза, называющая причину: The AI models aren't reachable right now — this is a search answer. The closest passages:. Под строками стоят Retry и Search the docs — та же пара, что предлагает транспортная ошибка: сбой мог уже пройти, цитата едет вместе с вопросом, а поиск никогда не зависел от модели. Ничего не сгенерировано, поэтому панели тут не в чем ошибиться. Два хода завершаются иначе, и оба верно: сбой до извлечения остаётся транспортной ошибкой The AI service didn't respond. со state: 'error', а исчерпанный дневной лимит держит state: 'rate-limited' и свой текст, потому что служба ответила расписанием; ближайшие пассажи перечислены и под ним, одними ссылками.

question: And what covers the ones it lets through?
prev_questions: How does the panel stop a reader from sending an API key to the model?
Which shapes does it catch?
gold_answer: Nothing in the browser does — what covers them is the instruction sent to the model. It carries matching rules: never echo a credential back, treat one that arrives as compromised, use placeholders in every code sample, and close with a line about keeping credentials out of committed source. Those rules cover exactly what the shape test declines to match, the bare UUID included. They are not the control, though, because by the time a model reads them the value has already been sent — the shape test is the only thing that acts before the question leaves the browser. And none of it is a security boundary. Everything runs in the reader's own browser, so it is a habit guard: it cannot stop a reader who pastes a key into a model directly, and it does not claim to.

question: And why does one of them jump the queue?
prev_questions: Why does the panel answer a greeting from a template instead of letting the gate refuse it?
What else does it claim besides a hello?
gold_answer: Identity does. "Hi, who are you" is a greeting and an identity question at once, so identity is matched ahead of greeting — the identity answer is the more useful of the two, and a reader asking what the assistant can do gets told rather than waved at. The other two, thanks and farewell, overlap with nothing and need no ordering. All four settle in the browser from shipped copy with no model call: the reply is a template, not a generation. The copy ships in eighteen languages, chosen by the same script-and-function-word detector the credential warning uses — the language the reader typed, not the locale of the page. A farewell carries no invitation and no suggestions; the other three do.

question: А если удалить один из них в одной вкладке?
prev_questions: Где панель хранит разговоры читателя?
Видит ли их вторая вкладка того же сайта?
Не затирают ли вкладки записи друг друга?
gold_answer: Строка исчезнет из списка в этой вкладке, а если удалённый разговор был открыт на экране, панель опустеет вместе с ним. Во второй вкладке он может вернуться: удаление разговора, с которым другая вкладка сейчас работает, отменяется, как только та записывает свой следующий оборот, — потому что каждая вкладка пишет, предварительно перечитав список, и так ни одна не стирает строки другой. Это сознательно выбранный из двух возможных отказ: альтернатива — вкладка, которая молча перестаёт сохранять что-либо до конца своей жизни. Список к тому же перечитывается в момент открытия переключателя, а не постоянно, поэтому соседняя вкладка какое-то время может показывать строку, которой уже нет. Удалить сразу все можно одной кнопкой: она очищает и список, и панель, спрашивает дважды и никогда не через диалог браузера.

question: And which of them is not a loss at all?
prev_questions: What does the panel write down for each turn of a conversation?
And what does it deliberately leave out?
What does that cost a reader who reopens the thread?
gold_answer: The rendered HTML. It is the one omission that costs nothing, because it is recomputed on restore rather than replayed — which is not only smaller to store but more correct: a link to a page that has since been deleted comes back as plain text instead of as a link into a 404. Answers are re-rendered against the current index, so rebuilding the index does not throw the archive away; an older conversation still opens, with one line above it saying the docs have changed and some links may no longer work. A source row underneath an answer behaves differently — it is a fixed address written at the time — so it can still point at a page that has gone. The other omissions do cost something: a restored turn has no reasoning disclosure, and a vote cast on one reports no retrieved ids.

question: And which of them change when the page goes dark?
prev_questions: How do I change the panel's colours without patching a component?
Where does my own CSS have to be loaded for that to work?
gold_answer: Nine of them, and only those nine: --dp-surface, --dp-surface-2, --dp-line, --dp-text, --dp-text-dim, --dp-on-text, --dp-focus, --dp-chip and --dp-code-bg. The core switches that set on prefers-color-scheme; everything that is not a colour — the geometry, the radii, the durations, the stacking value — is declared once, because it does not vary with appearance. --dp-wash and --dp-lip are left out of the dark block deliberately: both are derived from --dp-text through color-mix, so they follow it into dark without a second declaration, and neither may ever be given a dark variant of its own. --dp-accent-soft, --dp-shadow and --dp-scrim stay out for a different reason — one value reads on both schemes. The same nine are what ui.theme pins, declared again on a docpilot-dark class one step deeper than :root, and an adapter has to re-declare the whole colour set unconditionally instead of copying that media query.

question: Why not just remount it?
prev_questions: How do I mount the panel in a React app?
What do I have to pass so it keeps up with my router?
gold_answer: Because a remount would throw away the reader's conversation, and that conversation is the one thing the panel keeps across route changes on every other host. So route and lang are not a remount key: when they change, the new values are pushed into the running instance instead, and the thread stays where it was. There is little to re-create anyway. The component renders one empty div, and everything visible — the panel, the icon sprite, the selection popover — teleports to <body>, so where you place it in the tree does not decide where it appears. Place it once, high in the layout, and change its props from then on. Keep route base-less, /guide/install rather than /docs/guide/install, and if the site is served from a subdirectory say so once with base.

question: And what would it take to use the other one instead?
prev_questions: How do I install DocPilot on a Docusaurus site?
Where does the index have to be written?
What colours the code inside an answer?
gold_answer: Nothing the plugin can do for you — it has to be a client module of your own. Write a file that imports setHighlighter from @cloflin/docpilot/web and createPrismHighlighter from @cloflin/docpilot/prism, imports a Prism theme, and calls setHighlighter(createPrismHighlighter()); then list that file under clientModules in docusaurus.config.js. It cannot be a plugin option because webpack resolves dynamic imports at build time, so a module shipped inside this package that so much as named @cloflin/docpilot/hljs would fail the build of every site that has not installed highlight.js. In your own file, your own dependencies resolve. Importing the theme will not disturb your existing code blocks either: Prism scopes its block chrome under [class*="language-"], which this panel never emits, and Docusaurus paints its own blocks with inline styles, which win over a stylesheet anyway.

question: А что из этого вообще нельзя заменить?
prev_questions: Как перевести интерфейс панели на русский?
А если я задам только одну строку, остальные пропадут?
А что будет, если я ошибусь в названии ключа?
gold_answer: Три вещи. Первая — системная инструкция. promptHash называет каждый отчёт eval, а eval отказывается сравнивать два отчёта, собранных с разными инструкциями, так что переводимый промпт дал бы двум читателям одной и той же сборки разные хеши и сломал бы любое сравнение отчётов. Менять инструкцию нужно через prompt.override или prompt.extend — они действуют на сборке и существуют в единственном экземпляре, — а languageDirective и так заставляет модель отвечать на языке читателя, поэтому перевод промпта ничего не даёт и стоит хеша. Вторая — тела раскрытия промпта: это точные байты, отправленные модели, и перевод превратил бы раскрытие в описание чего-то другого. Заголовки над ними — обычный интерфейс, они в таблице как promptDoc.heading*. Третья — названия страниц и разделов: выбор области показывает текст корпуса, и переведённый заголовок назвал бы страницу, которой не существует.

question: And what does its path do, if it is not a route?
prev_questions: What is an imported page?
Which origins is it allowed to name as its source?
gold_answer: It has no route, so the path it carries in the manifest is an identifier that merely looks like one, and three things follow from that, all of them enforced rather than requested. manifest.pages[] records external: true for it. The source row and the [n] citation marker open the origin instead, in a new tab and with rel="noopener noreferrer", because the answer is rendered as HTML and an opened tab that keeps window.opener can navigate the panel it came from. And the id is absent from the set of routes a link may point at, so a model link to it is de-linked rather than rendered as an anchor to a 404 — the reader still reads the sentence, and the only live link to that material is its source row. A page inside docsDir may carry a source as well, and that one keeps its route while the citation row opens the original.

question: And why is the last one worded separately?
prev_questions: What does a build warn about when a block is too big to fit in one chunk?
What should I do about the second one?
gold_answer: Because it is the only one of the three where the structure could not be preserved. The other two repair themselves: a fence over the ceiling is closed at the cut and reopened on the next part with the same characters, indent and info string, and a table split at row boundaries re-emits its header and delimiter on every continuation. The third fires when a single row did not fit even with the header re-emitted, so it was cut mid-row, and what lands in the index is half a row with nothing to attach it to. That usually means one cell is carrying a payload — a base64 blob, a stack trace, a paragraph — and the fix is to move it out of the table rather than to shorten the table. Like the other two it is a warn line naming the file, measured against the same MAX_CHUNK_CHARS ceiling, and none of the three fails the build.

question: And when it carries none at all?
prev_questions: How much of the golden set does an eval run measure?
Do the tiers stack, or is each one its own list?
What happens to a record whose tier is misspelled?
gold_answer: Then it reads as high. That default exists so tiers could arrive on a golden file that already existed without moving a number: high is defined as roughly the set this package was developed against, so a file written before tiers scores identically under --level=high and under no flag at all, and nobody has to backfill sixty records to keep their history comparable. npx docpilot lint treats it as a warning rather than an error, which is the opposite of a value that is none of the six tiers — that one is an error, and at run time it falls into every pool, the smoke one included. The matching default on the other side is the run itself: with no --level given, a run is ultra, the whole file, which is what every run did before tiers existed.

question: And why is the second of those the serious one?
prev_questions: What does npx docpilot index --no-embed build?
Is that the same as declaring it in the config?
What does doctor say when the two disagree?
gold_answer: Because that pairing cannot work at all, where the other one merely wastes bytes. A vectorless index under a config that still names an embedder means the deployment would embed every question and then have nothing to score the query vector against, so readiness refuses it and the build emits {enabled: false} — the panel is not rendered on the page at all. The reverse case ships a vector blob no reader will ever use: the site is heavier than it needs to be and everything works, so it is reported as a note. The practical consequence is that reaching for --no-embed on its own switches the panel off until the config agrees, either by saying embed: false too or by declaring embed.fallback: 'lexical', which is that same vectorless mode reached by refusal instead of by declaration.

question: кстати, а как в PostgreSQL сделать индекс по jsonb-полю?
prev_questions: Как перевести интерфейс панели на русский?
А что перевести нельзя?
А как русский вопрос вообще находит ответ в английских доках?
